page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.c7a.16xlarge is a compute-optimized virtual server instance powered by the KVM hypervisor. It features 64 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 32 physical cores of an AMD EPYC 7T83 processor running at 2.55 GHz. The system is equipped with 128.0 GB of system memory, yielding a compute-focused ratio of 2.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. The x86_64 architecture supports hardware-level features such as AVX, AES, VAES, SHA_NI, and FMA. This instance does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware, relying instead on network-attached storage and a baseline network bandwidth of 16 Gbps.

Benchmark evaluations indicate strong performance characteristics, particularly in multi-threaded and compute-heavy workloads. The instance achieves top-tier results in stress-ng single-core and multi-core CPU tests, as well as PassMark CPU, extended instructions, and encryption tests. Memory performance is mixed; while small-block cached read-only memory bandwidth is strong, large-block uncached read and write operations fall into the average tier. Multi-threaded bzip3 decompression, Geekbench ray tracing, and image processing benchmarks also demonstrate strong performance, whereas software compilation and text processing remain average.

In database and transactional workloads, the ecs.c7a.16xlarge performs exceptionally well, as evidenced by strong scores in PassMark database operations and Redis SET operations. It also shows strong capability in low-parameter language model inference, though performance drops to average levels when processing medium-sized 7B models. Given the absence of local storage and a 1:2 RAM-to-vCPU ratio, this instance is highly cost-efficient for CPU-bound tasks like ray tracing, image processing, and high-throughput database operations, but is less suited for memory-intensive applications or workloads requiring high-speed local NVMe storage.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.c7a.16xlarge is a compute-optimized virtual server powered by the KVM hypervisor and an AMD EPYC 7T83 processor. It features 64 dedicated vCPUs, 32 physical cores, and 128.0 GB of RAM, establishing a 2.0 GB per vCPU ratio. The instance lacks local storage and GPUs but provides a 16 Gbps baseline network bandwidth. Benchmark data shows strong performance in multi-core CPU stress tests, PassMark encryption, and Redis SET operations, alongside strong small-block memory bandwidth. However, uncached large-block memory operations and software compilation fall into average performance tiers. The server is highly suited for compute-intensive workloads, multi-threaded decompression, and high-throughput database operations, offering a balanced, resource-dense profile for CPU-bound tasks without the overhead of local storage.
